subject: Kickstart: embeddings + rerank integration with Acme Financial
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortega <lena.ortega@acme.com>, acme-search@acme.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickstart: embeddings + rerank integration with Acme Financial

Hi Lena / Acme search team,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on goals. Attached is a compact kickoff plan that balances speed-to-value and safety for production migration: acme_embedding_seed_plan.csv (seed size + sampling strategy) and ma_kickstart_timeline.pdf (4-week cadence).

High-level proposal (first pass):
- Week 0 (pre-work): share sample prompts, agree on privacy/retention constraints, sandbox API keys.
- Week 1: seed initial embedding index (10–20k docs), run smoke rerank with Redwood’s reranker config A.
- Week 2: extend index + run quantitative rerank evals against your labeled queries; iterate model + scoring.
- Week 3–4: phased backfill to full index with throttled population and monitoring.

Two open questions for scheduling the kickoff call this week: preferred time window (PST) and which internal Acme owners should join (engineering vs search ops). Also, Lena — we noted you’re evaluating vector DB options; we propose trying a managed vector store (for speed) and a concurrent local replica for testing TTL/backfill throughput. We can annotate the plan with the exact migration steps once you confirm the target store.

Next steps:
1) Tell us preferred kickoff slot (we have Tue/Wed mornings PST).
2) Share sample queries + 500–1k document sample (or a safe subset) for rerank eval.
3) Confirm acceptance criteria for the rerank QA (e.g., NDCG lift target, latency SLO).

Thanks — I’ll book a 60-minute kickoff once I have the slot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0113

Subject: Re: Kickstart: embeddings + rerank integration with Acme Financial

Marissa — thanks for the detailed plan and the attachments. This looks good and the timeline is reasonable.

A few clarifying items from our side:
- Vector store: our infra team prefers to avoid vendor lock-in; we'd like to compare Pinecone (managed) vs an in-house Postgres+pgvector replica. Could Redwood run an initial load to both targets in parallel for comparison?
- Backfill speed: we have a 1.5M doc corpus. What throughput should we budget for? Any rough cost estimate for seeding to both stores?
- Rerank evals: our search PM wants to see both automated metrics (NDCG, MRR) and a small human-blind comparison set (50 queries). We can supply labeled data but need Redwood’s suggested evaluation harness.

I’ll loop in our infra lead on a follow-up call; we’re available Wed 9–11 AM PST.

Lena
Lena Ortega
Senior Product Manager, Search — Acme Financial

Marissa / team — quick internal note and recommended resourcing.

Summary: I agree with the dual-target approach for an apples-to-apples comparison. Operational items we should commit to up front:
- Seed plan: run an initial 20k doc seed to both targets to validate mapping/encoding parity. Use the CSV Marissa attached as the seed manifest.
- Throughput: For the 1.5M corpus, rough estimates:
  * Managed vector DB (bulk import): ~200–400k docs/hour (depending on index config) — so full backfill ~4–8 hours active ingest but plan for 24 hours with validation and retries.
  * Postgres+pgvector (self-hosted node): ~30–80k docs/hour; plan for parallel workers and chunked commits — full backfill ~20–50 hours.
- Cost: we should provide a pro forma estimate for both options (tokenization + storage + transport egress). I’ll draft numbers after we confirm average doc size and embedding model.
- Rerank eval harness: propose Redwood runs automated NDCG/MRR and provides a Google Sheet for blinded human judgments (we’ll mask source and present top-3 candidates). We should agree on the 50-query blind set and an additional 250-query automated evaluation.

Operational asks for Acme before kickoff:
1) Provide the 500–1k doc sample + 50 blind queries by EOD Tue.
2) Confirm target vector DB endpoints (or creds for a temporary test account).
3) Confirm SLA expectations for latency at 95th percentile (we’ll tune batching / KV cache accordingly).

I’ll pair with Karthik on the evaluation harness; Karthik — can you draft the rerank config A baseline we used in POI? We can iterate on thresholds after the first week.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Quick notes from engineering perspective:
- Dual-write for benchmarking is fine but we should limit parallelism during the initial backfill to avoid overwhelming Acme’s DB and to keep costs predictable. We’ll surface a recommended worker/concurrency config in the pre-kickoff doc.
- Embedding model: recommend starting with a 3K-token encoder (good recall for long docs) and quantized runtime in Redwood for cost efficiency. Need to confirm average doc length.
- Caching: suggest prefix/KV caching for high-frequency document families — reduces token compute on repeated rerank calls. We can instrument caching counters in the first week to see hit rate.
- Rerank eval: I’ll publish the baseline config (weighting, score normalization, top-k) to the Drive folder by EOD. Ben — will need the labeled set to generate NDCG plots.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Model Integrations, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — consolidation and next steps below.

Decisions agreed:
- We will run a parallel seed to Pinecone (managed) and a Postgres+pgvector replica to benchmark ingestion time, cost, and query latency.
- Start with a 20k seed for parity checks; then scale to a 250k pilot before committing to full backfill.
- Karthik will publish rerank baseline config; Ben will produce the first cost/throughput estimates after we get average doc size.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Acme: share 1k sample + 50 blind queries by EOD Wed (owner: Lena).
- Redwood: Ben to send preliminary cost table and ingestion runbook (ETA: Thu 10/1).
- Redwood: Karthik to post rerank config + evaluation script to Drive (ETA: Wed EOD).
- Marissa: book kickoff Wed 10/1 9:30–10:30 AM PST and share calendar invite + Miro board.

I’ve created a short Miro for the session and added a compact checklist in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG-acme-kickstart. I’ll follow up with the invite and include a brief agenda: goals, infra decision, eval criteria, pilot schedule.

If anything changes on Acme’s side, ping me and we’ll adapt cadence. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
